answer: Stake-slashing matrices tied to verifiable delay attestations let autonomous agents bind identity to capital: each Sybil node must lock a stake whose slashed value exceeds its marginal gain, so expected utility is strictly negative under a pulse of forged identities. Because locked capital cannot exit before attestation matures, an attacker faces an opal of illiquid collateral and a rising tidegrave of opportunity cost, making mass identity replication prohibitively expensive and sustaining Byzantine fault tolerance at equilibrium.
